{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABYqonQQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhCPlkQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 11, "title": "Update Gene Light comparison demo to three-mmd 0.1.1", "body": "## Problem

The Gene Light side-by-side comparison demo currently pins `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.0`, while the upstream [three-mmd-loader](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader) package now declares **0.1.1**. Update the demo to use 0.1.1, verify its behavior, and retain the existing PMX-to-glTF comparison.

## Expected outcome

The left-hand **direct PMX reference** in the public [mmd-gltf demo](https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/) uses `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.1`. The right-hand converted GLB still uses the existing `MMD_materials_toon` GLTFLoader plugin. Both views remain comparable.

## Context

- Current dependency: `package.json` and `package-lock.json` in [mmd-gltf](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf) specify `@takahirox/three-mmd: 0.1.0`.
- The [upstream package.json](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/package.json) specifies `0.1.1` and a `three: ~0.186.0` peer dependency.
- The existing example, [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts), loads the direct PMX with `MMDLoader` alongside a generated glTF model.
- The initial visual comparison, [`docs/comparison.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/comparison.md), records remaining shading differences and matched-view screenshots.

## Implementation

1. Update `@takahirox/three-mmd` from **0.1.0 to 0.1.1** in `package.json` and the lockfile. Verify that the published package is resolvable and that only one compatible copy of Three.js is installed.
2. Adapt the demo or integration **only if necessary** for 0.1.1 compatibility. Do not change the `MMD_materials_toon` specification or the PMX converter just to make the reference look more similar.
3. Preserve the two aligned static/base-pose Gene Light views, synchronized camera and zoom, Front/Side/Back presets, WebGL2 support, the glTF toon/PBR toggle, and all model attribution/rights notices.
4. Exercise real rendered output from the updated reference, using matched screenshots (at least front and side) and inspect for obvious new geometry, material, texture, alpha or orientation regressions. Update comparison documentation if the appearance meaningfully changes; do not require pixel-identical output.
5. Update any version references in documentation and tests. Keep the change focused on this dependency upgrade and necessary compatibility fixes.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] `package.json` and `package-lock.json` consistently resolve `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.1`; `npm ci` succeeds and `npm ls three @takahirox/three-mmd` reports one compatible Three.js installation.
- [ ] The built Gene Light comparison demo loads the original PMX through the **0.1.1 MMDLoader** and displays it next to the converted GLB; no asset/network/runtime/shader errors are introduced.
- [ ] Both model views retain matched pose, scale, camera, lighting, synchronized navigation and view presets. glTF toon/PBR switching and existing Gene Light credits/notices continue to work.
- [ ] Real browser-rendered front/side comparison captures are inspected for regressions and any required compatibility fixes are made; noteworthy visual changes are documented with evidence.
- [ ] Existing type, unit, glTF extension conformance, converter, browser, static build and link checks pass using the repository's documented commands. Report any skips accurately.
- [ ] Do not introduce unrelated material-spec changes, new extensions, or broader refactoring.

Suggested checks: `npm ci`, `npm ls three @takahirox/three-mmd`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check`. Document actual results rather than assuming success.

## Optional validation

Check native WebGPU output if a supported adapter is available. Lack of a native adapter is not a blocker when WebGL2 checks pass.

## Required post-merge verification

After the `main` merge and GitHub Pages deployment, open https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/ and verify the updated direct PMX reference, paired GLB, navigation/toggles, and asset/console health. Record the deployed commit and workflow result. This publication check takes place after merge and is not a pre-merge gate.
